+        # input text preprocessing: identical chunks always evolve identically,
+        # so keep each unique chunk once (in first-occurrence order, which keeps
+        # the pair insertion order and thus max() tie-breaking unchanged) and
+        # weight it by its frequency
+        weights = {}
+        for ch in text_chunks:
+            weights[ch] = weights.get(ch, 0) + 1
+        ids = [list(ch.encode("utf-8")) for ch in weights]
+        counts = list(weights.values())
+        # chunks with fewer than 2 ids contribute no pairs; drop them
+        keep = [j for j in range(len(ids)) if len(ids[j]) >= 2]
+        ids = [ids[j] for j in keep]
+        counts = [counts[j] for j in keep]
+
+        # iteratively merge the most common pairs to create new tokens
+        merges = {} # (int, int) -> int
+        vocab = {idx: bytes([idx]) for idx in range(256)} # idx -> bytes
+        for i in range(num_merges):
+            # count the number of times every consecutive pair appears
+            stats = {}
+            get = stats.get
+            for chunk_ids, w in zip(ids, counts):

+                    stats[p] = get(p, 0) + w
+            # find the pair with the highest count
+            pair = max(stats, key=stats.get)
+            # mint a new token: assign it the next available id
+            idx = 256 + i
+            # replace all occurrences of pair in ids with idx
+            a, b = pair
+            new_ids = []
+            new_counts = []
+            for chunk_ids, w in zip(ids, counts):
+                if a in chunk_ids:
+                    chunk_ids = merge(chunk_ids, pair, idx)
+                    if len(chunk_ids) < 2:
+                        continue
+                new_ids.append(chunk_ids)
+                new_counts.append(w)
+            ids = new_ids
+            counts = new_counts

actions.reason: RegexTokenizer.train now deduplicates regex chunks, keeping them in first-occurrence order, and weights each unique chunk by how often it appears. Identical chunks always evolve identically under merges. The pairs are first met in the same order as before, so stats dict insertion order, counts and max() tie-breaking are all unchanged. Chunks with fewer than 2 ids contribute no pairs and are dropped. Merge is skipped for chunks that do not contain the pair's first id. Outputs were identical on the equivalence harness, and train_regex_ir ratio was 0.344.

journal.text:
I changed RegexTokenizer.train in minbpe/regex.py (lines 43-60, 18 lines replaced by 41). It now deduplicates regex chunks in first-occurrence order and weights each unique chunk by its count. Identical chunks evolve identically under merges, so I expected the stats insertion order, counts and max() tie-breaking to stay the same. Chunks with fewer than 2 ids are dropped since they contribute no pairs.

My sandbox run was accepted with identical outputs and guards ok over 1 file and 35 lines. train_regex_ir went from 6738778738 to 2317441554, ratio 0.3439. The other metrics stayed flat: train_basic_ir 0.9974, encode_ir 1.0009, decode_ir 1.0007, save_load_ir 1.0010. I submitted it, and it is committed and queued for independent replay.

I believe regex training was dominated by redundant per-chunk work on repeated chunks. Weighted counting removes most of that without changing results.

Next I would look at encode_ir. Repeated chunks could be cached there the same way, and I would also check whether merge application in train can be made incremental.
